title: Doghouse Shuffles
subtitle: Lose to enter. Score to escape. Keep the heat on.

hero.alt: A Doghouse Shuffle session in progress, showing the escape target, the loss limit and the round schedule

intro: Lose a game and you are in the doghouse. Get back out by scoring your way clear — and if you cannot, the loss limit eventually ejects you. It is continuous play with a running consequence, which is what stops a social session drifting into pat-ball.

Set the escape points and the loss limit, and TournaQ runs the rest: who is on court, who is queuing, who has just gone in and who has just got out. Every player carries their own record, so the ranking at the end is individual.
bestfor: Sessions with a competitive edge where nobody wants an easy game
Groups that want continuous play with no downtime between rounds
Anywhere a bit of jeopardy makes people try harder

sections.title: Finding it in the app
sections.text: Doghouse Shuffles lives under Single Competitions & Socials in the TournaQ Arena. The hub keeps every session you have run, so last week's is two taps away.

cards.alt: The TournaQ Arena, with every format grouped by the kind of session it suits
cards.p: Every format the app can run, grouped by the kind of session it suits. The number on a card is how many of those you have run.
New Tournament starts a session. Below it sits your history, each entry showing the date, the player count and how far it got.
cards.alt: The Doghouse Shuffles hub listing past sessions above a New Tournament button

sections.title: Setting it up
sections.text: Two numbers define a Doghouse Shuffle: how many points get you out, and how many losses put you out for good. Everything else is the usual — players, courts, time.

p: Escape points and the loss limit sit alongside players, courts, rounds and match duration. Change any of them and the Schedule Preview re-does the sums, so the predicted finish time moves as you decide how long you want to play.
Set the escape target low and the doghouse empties fast; set it high and people stay in it, which is usually where the shouting starts.
cards.alt: The complete Doghouse Shuffle setup form, from players and courts through escape points and the loss limit

cards.p: Add players by name, pull them from your saved Players hub, or fill the session with random names to try the format out. The list is editable all the way through the session, not just at the start.
cards.alt: The player sheet listing everyone in the session with their games played and points

sections.title: The session at a glance
sections.text: Once it starts, one screen carries the session: how far along you are, who is on which court, who is sitting out, and when you will be done.

cards.h: Progress and settings in one row
cards.p: Rounds complete, a progress ring, and a row of pills — standings, allocation, players, format, escape points, loss limit and estimated finish. A pill with a pencil can still be changed; one with a lock was fixed when play started.
cards.alt: Doghouse Shuffle overview showing one of four rounds complete, a 25% ring and the settings pills

cards.h: Round by round, or court by court
cards.p: The schedule groups by round out of the box. Switch it to Court and each court lists its own sequence instead — the view to hand someone refereeing one court all session.
cards.alt: The Doghouse Shuffle schedule regrouped so each court lists its own matches

cards.p: The allocation grid lays every round against every court. It is the whole session on one screen, and the place you notice someone has been sitting out too often.
cards.alt: A grid of rounds against courts showing which players are assigned where

sections.title: Scoring a match
sections.text: The scorecard is built for one hand at the side of a court: big targets, the running score, and the rotation handled for you as games finish.

cards.p: Tap a side to award the point. The timer runs in the header, the doghouse state is visible on the card, and undo takes back the last point when the call goes the other way.
cards.alt: The Doghouse Shuffle scorecard in portrait with the running score and the session timer

cards.p: Turn the phone and the same controls rearrange for a net post or a table at the side of the court. Nothing is hidden — the layout changes, the functions do not.
cards.alt: The same Doghouse Shuffle scorecard rotated to landscape

cards.p: When a game ends the next players are rotated in automatically and the card tells you who is up. Nobody has to remember whose turn it was.
cards.alt: A dialog confirming that the next players have rotated onto court

sections.title: Into the doghouse, and out again
sections.text: The two moments that define the format, and TournaQ announces both so the court knows where it stands without anyone keeping count.

cards.p: Score your way to the escape target and you are out, back into normal play with a clean slate. The dialog names who got out, so the rest of the court knows the pecking order has changed.
cards.alt: A dialog announcing that a player has escaped the doghouse

cards.p: Hit the loss limit and you are ejected from the session. Games already played still count towards the ranking, so a bad run does not erase what came before it.
cards.alt: A dialog announcing that a player has been ejected after reaching the loss limit

sections.title: Standings, live and final
sections.text: Every player carries their own record, so the ranking is individual even though the teams change all session.

cards.p: Every player with their points, games played and win record, ordered as it stands right now. Players check it between rounds without asking anyone.
cards.alt: Live individual standings partway through the session

cards.p: When the last game is in, the table closes with the winner at the top — the player who spent the least time in the doghouse and the most time scoring.
cards.alt: The final ranking table at the end of the session

cards.p: The schedule keeps every result. A completed session stays in the hub with all its scores, so a question about last month's session has an answer.
cards.alt: A completed session with every round played and every score recorded

workflow: Open the TournaQ Arena and pick Doghouse Shuffles.
Set the players, courts and match length, then the escape points and the loss limit.
Add the players and name the session.
Open the first match and start the timer.
Tap a side to award each point; undo takes back the last one.
Finish the game — the next players rotate on automatically.
Watch for the escape and ejection announcements as the session runs.
Play out the rounds and read the final rankings.
